issue_context.title: [BUG] locator picker in trace viewer behaves differently to the one in the playwright inspector
issue_context.body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do not delete this template ⚠️⚠️ -->

<!-- 🔎 Search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->
<!-- 🧪 Test using the latest Playwright release to see if your issue has already been fixed -->
<!-- 💡 Provide enough information for us to be able to reproduce your issue locally -->

### System info
- Playwright Version: 1.32.0-alpha-mar-3-2023
- Operating System: windows 10
- Browser: chromium
- Other info:

### Source code

- [X] I provided exact source code that allows reproducing the issue locally.

<!-- For simple cases, please provide a self-contained test file along with the config file -->
<!-- For larger cases, you can provide a GitHub repo you created for this issue -->
<!-- If we can not reproduce the problem locally, we won't be able to act on it -->
<!-- You can still file without the exact code and we will try to help, but if we can't repro, it will be closed -->

**Config file**

```ts
// playwright.config.ts
import type { PlaywrightTestConfig } from '@playwright/test'
import { devices } from '@playwright/test'

const config: PlaywrightTestConfig = {
    testDir: './tests',
    timeout: 50 * 1000,
    expect: {
        timeout: 50000,
    },
    forbidOnly: !!process.env['CI'],
    retries: process.env['CI'] ? 2 : 0,
    reporter: 'html',
    use: {
        actionTimeout: 0,
        trace: 'on',
    },
    projects: [
        {
            name: 'chromium',
            use: {
                ...devices['Desktop Chrome'],
            },
        },
    ],
}

export default config
```

**Test file (self-contained)**

```js
test('asdf', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('https://google.com')
    await page.pause()
})
```

**Steps**
1. run `playwright test`
1. hit run button when the inspector appears
1. when it pauses, input the locator, eg. `//span`
1. hit resume button
1. run `playwright show-report` then click the trace button on the test
1. input the same locator as before, eg. `//span`

**Expected**
the same elements are highlighted in both the inspector and the trace viewer

**Actual**
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/57028336/222626784-07f775ae-3613-432a-a10c-854d78ca03b9.png)
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/57028336/222626964-f64f5d93-032f-4924-aa79-1729317d3546.png)

review_comments: Should we add `Document/Node` to the list of prohibited globals?
I did at first, but I could not find a way to ban it only as a runtime object - it yells at all the type declarations...
